## ✨ Highlights

- 🧭 **The Controller manages your nodes' Consul agents**: give it your Consul cluster's address and a token, and every node with the `consul` extension becomes a client of that cluster with its own ACL token - the datacenter, the servers and the gossip key are read from Consul, never typed ([#400](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/400), [Consul through the Controller](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/consul-controller.md)).
- 📡 **Nodes register what they serve**: janusd, every exporter that runs - where it really listens -, each HAProxy frontend, and one entry per URL its maps and Host ACLs route. Prometheus finds the exporters by the `prometheus` tag and has the blackbox exporter probe the URLs ([Prometheus: the exporters and the URLs](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/consul-controller.md#prometheus-the-exporters-and-the-urls)).
- 🏷️ **Hypervisors have labels, and their nodes inherit them**: label a hypervisor `dc=lgs room=r1`, and every node the Controller made on it carries those labels - its own win on a clash ([#401](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/401), [Labels: where a hypervisor is](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/hypervisors.md#labels-where-a-hypervisor-is)).

## 🧭 Consul

- **On the Controller** ([#400](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/400)): a **Consul** tab next to Log forwarding and Let's Encrypt (admins).
  - The settings: the cluster's HTTPS address and how to trust it (a CA, a fingerprint or the system's), a token, the servers' RPC CA, which nodes (a label selector - every node with the extension when empty) and which services they register.
  - **Test** says in words what works and what doesn't: the address, the token's rights, the datacenter it found.
  - The Controller makes a `janus-nodes` policy and one token per node (its node identity + that policy), and keeps them sealed with its master key. A token deleted in Consul is made again.
  - A node removed from the Controller, out of the selector or without the extension any more loses its layer, its token, and its entry in the catalog.
  - A table says, for each node, where its layer is, whether its agent is alive and how many services and URLs it registered.
  - The node's labels - its inherited ones included - go into its `node_meta`, with `janus_node_id` and `janus_cluster` for a cluster member.
  - `GET/PUT /api/consul`, `POST /api/consul/test`, `POST /api/consul/run`, `GET /api/consul/nodes` ([The API](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/consul-controller.md#the-api)).
- **On the node**:
  - `NetworkService/ConsulManagedGet` (readers - the token and the gossip key are never returned) and `ConsulManagedSet` (admins): the layer a Controller manages - or your own orchestrator - beside your own configuration of the agent, whose keys it overrides.
  - The agent runs with the layer alone. It restarts only when what it reads changed.
  - Its token and the gossip key are kept on STATE in a file no file RPC serves, and travel in a state transfer only with the node's identity.
- **The node registers its own services** in its agent, under IDs starting with `janus:` - your own `services {}` are never touched:
  - `janus` (its API) and every exporter that runs, at the address it really listens on, with the tag `prometheus` and their `metrics_path` and `scheme`: `janus-exporter`, `node-exporter`, and `haproxy-exporter` for a frontend serving HAProxy's own Prometheus exporter. An exporter turned off or moved follows within seconds.
  - `haproxy-<frontend>` for each frontend and listen section, with a TCP check.
  - `haproxy-url`: one instance per host a frontend routes - the keys of a map read through the Host header (or the TLS SNI), and Host ACLs' values. A map changed at runtime shows in Consul about a second later. IPs, wildcards and regexes are left out.
  - A drained node, an HAProxy stopped, or a node going down puts these services in maintenance; undrained, they're back.
- **Where to see them**: the node's **Apps › Consul** page lists the agent's services - address, tags, URL or metrics path, health with the check's output, declared by Janus or by the configuration - filtered by kind. `janusctl network consul services` prints the same; `janusctl network consul managed` shows the layer.
- **Status with ACLs**: the node's Consul page and `ConsulStatus` use the layer's token, so they show the members and services of a cluster whose ACLs deny anonymous reads.
- **Prometheus**: `examples/prometheus/consul.yml` - a job scraping every service tagged `prometheus` and a blackbox job probing every `haproxy-url` ([Discovery through Consul](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/metrics.md#discovery-through-consul)).

## 🏷️ Labels

- **A hypervisor's labels** ([#401](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/401)): in its form ("Labels its nodes inherit" - `dc`, `room`, `rack` suggested), on its card, in `POST`/`PATCH /api/hypervisors`, and on Terraform's `janus_hypervisor` and `janus_proxmox_hypervisor`.
- **A machine's node inherits them**, read at once - nothing is copied, so a change on the hypervisor follows on every node. The node's own labels win on the same key. Its card shows the inherited ones read-only beside its own; `/api/nodes` returns `inherited_labels` and `inherited_from`; Terraform's `janus_node.labels` still owns only the node's own, and `inherited_labels` reads the others.
- Everything that picks nodes by label uses the inherited ones too: grants, scoped API tokens, SSO rules, janusctl's scoped certificates, log forwarding profiles, and Consul's `node_meta`.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Labelling a hypervisor widens label-based access**: a grant, a scoped token or an SSO rule on `dc=lgs` reaches every node made on a hypervisor labelled `dc=lgs` as soon as it is labelled. Check your selectors before labelling hypervisors.
- **The Consul integration is off until you turn it on**. It needs a Consul cluster with ACLs, and a token with `acl = "write"`, `keyring = "read"` and `operator = "read"` - a token that can make any token: keep it as an admin secret ([Before you start](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/consul-controller.md#before-you-start)). The servers must reach every node on 8301 (TCP and UDP), and the nodes the servers on 8300 and 8301 - and each other on 8301.
- **A node you configured by hand**: once the Controller manages it, the layer's keys win over yours (datacenter, servers, gossip key, ACL tokens, TLS, `node_meta`); your services and other settings stay.
- **Nodes on an earlier release** show as unsupported in the Consul tab until they're updated.
